newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Arabia awards King Faisal prizes.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia awards King Faisal prizes.

text.p: Saudi Arabia awarded on Tuesday King Faisal International Prizes to Malaysia's prime minister, an Iraqi doctor and five Western scientists, an official statement said.
The awards will be handed out at a ceremony held under the patronage of Saudi Arabia's King Fahd next month, said the statement by the General Secretariat administering the prize.
Each prize, which Saudi Arabia started granting to scientists and Islamic scholars in 1981, is worth 750,000 riyals ($200,000).
The prize for services to Islam went to Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad.
The prize for Islamic studies went to Doctor Abdul-Karim Zeedan Baheej Alani of Iraq for his study on the status of women in Islam.

The prize for medicine was shared by professors Colin Louis Masters of Australia, Konrad Traugott Beyreuther of Germany, James Francis Gusella of Canada for their studies on degenerative diseases of the nervous system.
Professor Carl E. Wieman and Doctor Eric A. Cornell, both Americans teaching at the University of Colorado, shared the science prize for their work in physics.
The statement said there was no prize this year for Arabic literature because of "insufficient merit."
